title: Strife
note: Of anger and desire, anger is the greater danger for rulers, so he begins with what anger brings. First comes strife: the discord that makes two sides fight and wear out their strength.

couplets.plain: They call strife the disease that feeds, in every living being, the fault of drawing apart.
couplets.pm: The learned call strife the fault that feeds, in all beings, the evil trait of not coming together with others. “Every living being” shows that it puts humans on a level with animals. It is called division because it comes between people and produces a divided nature.

links.reason: Calls strife the disease that feeds division in every living being.

links.quote: the disease that feeds, in every living being, the fault of drawing apart
links.reason: Frames strife as a disease that spreads division through all that lives.

couplets.plain: Even if someone means to break with you and does what you can’t bear, it is best not to answer with harm out of strife.
couplets.pm: Even if someone wants to break with you and does things you dislike, the highest course is not to do him harm in order to fight him. If you do, enmity grows and you sink. If you hold back, his hostile acts die away by themselves and you rise.

links.quote: it is best not to answer with harm
links.reason: Rules out answering with harm, even against someone who injures you on purpose.
Asks that harm not be returned, even when the other began it.
Speaks to someone set on a break with you, and says not to answer with harm.

couplets.plain: Get rid of the painful disease called strife, and you gain an undying, spotless brightness.
couplets.pm: If you remove from your mind the painful disease called strife, that removal gives you the fame that makes you live forever. Everyone becomes your friend, so you gain all wealth, and giving and the like bring you fame.

links.reason: Promises undying brightness to whoever gets rid of strife.

links.quote: Get rid of the painful disease
links.reason: Treats strife as a sickness you can be rid of.

couplets.plain: When strife, the worst pain of all pains, is gone, it brings the greatest joy of all joys.
couplets.pm: If you are free of strife, the greatest of all pains, that freedom gives you the greatest of all joys. The worst pain is fighting many, losing your strength and lying at everyone’s mercy, and strife brings this directly. The greatest joy is that everyone becomes a friend and you gain every benefit.

links.quote: strife, the worst pain of all pains
links.reason: Ranks strife the worst of all pains, and its end the greatest joy.

couplets.plain: Who would try to get the better of those who can turn aside from strife?
couplets.pm: When discord arises, some can refuse to take it up and turn aside. Who would think of defeating them? Giving up strife is hard in every way for rulers, so he says “can”. Such people are friends to all, so no one thinks of beating them.

links.quote: those who can turn aside from strife
links.reason: Shows the safety of the opposite: nobody tries to beat those who turn aside from strife.

couplets.plain: Someone who calls it sweet to press on in strife will soon see his life falter and fall to ruin.
couplets.pm: A man who says it is sweet to go further and further in strife, meaning to win, and keeps at it, has failure and total ruin close by. Failure means the misery of poverty. Total ruin means death. Loss of wealth and loss of life come at once.

links.quote: calls it sweet to press on in strife
links.reason: Relish for strife means the ruin of your own life is close.

couplets.plain: People of bitter understanding who cling to strife can’t see the truth that brings victory.
couplets.pm: People of harmful understanding, who keep to strife, can’t grasp what the books of statecraft teach, which brings victory. Such understanding hurts themselves and others. Those books are called true because those who follow the path to victory can see what they yield. Strife confuses the understanding, so they can’t see it.

links.quote: can’t see the truth that brings victory
links.reason: A taste for strife blinds people of bitter understanding to the truth that brings victory.

couplets.plain: Turning aside from strife brings gain. Press on with it, and ruin presses on towards you.
couplets.pm: When strife arises in your heart, refusing to take it up is gain. If you don’t refuse, and set about increasing it, ruin sets about coming to you. Gain comes the moment you turn aside, so he calls turning aside itself gain.

links.reason: Press on in strife, and ruin presses on to meet you.

links.quote: Turning aside from strife brings gain

couplets.plain: When gain is coming to him, a man doesn’t look for strife. To bring about his own ruin, he looks to increase it.
couplets.pm: When gain is coming to a man, he doesn’t think of strife even with cause. When he is bringing ruin on himself, he thinks of increasing it even without cause. “Bring about” shows that the ruin comes through his strife, not through others. Whether strife is absent or present tells you in advance whether gain or ruin is coming.

links.quote: To bring about his own ruin, he looks to increase it
links.reason: Reads a wish to increase strife as the sign that a man is already headed for ruin.

couplets.plain: Strife brings all that is bitter. Smiles bring the pride of true goodness.
couplets.pm: Strife alone brings every bitter thing, such as poverty, blame and sin. Friendship alone brings the great wealth called good policy. By “smiles” he means the friendship that causes them, and by “pride” the wealth that causes it.

links.quote: Strife brings all that is bitter

ideaLinks.quote: feeds, in every living being, the fault of drawing apart
ideaLinks.reason: Strife feeds the habit of drawing apart from others, which is the start of enmity.
